summary: You can now flip what is picked left to right or top to bottom: Flip Horizontal and Flip Vertical are on its right-click menu and in Edit > Transform, and dragging a side handle past the opposite side flips it and keeps going. Before, the right-click menu had no flip and the drag stopped at a box 1 point wide.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Before: a rectangle's right-click menu had no Flip row, and dragging its right handle past its left edge left it 1 point wide.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drop a picture on a canvas, right-click it and choose Flip Horizontal.
Choose Edit > Transform > Flip Vertical, then press Command Z: only the second flip comes off.
Type some words, pick them and choose Edit > Transform > Flip Horizontal: they read mirrored.
Pick the picture and drag its right handle past its left edge, then keep going.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick two layers and flip them together: they swap sides about the middle of both.
On a video, type a title, right-click it and choose Flip Horizontal, then step a second on: it is still mirrored, and the export is too.

evaluate: Is the right-click menu the right home for the pair, in their own section under Send to Back, or would you rather have them in a Transform submenu?
Does dragging a handle past the other side feel like Photoshop's Free Transform, with the picture mirrored the moment the edge crosses?
With several layers picked, is flipping about the middle of all of them (they swap sides) what you expected, rather than each one flipping in place?
Should Flip have keys? Photoshop gives the pair none, so none here; Figma uses Shift H and Shift V.
rough: No mock covers flipping; the placement follows Photoshop (Edit > Transform, no keys, UX-PATTERNS §7) and Figma's flat right-click rows.
While a handle drag is past the other side the magnets (grid, guides, other layers' edges) do not pull; they pull again once it comes back.
A picture being dragged past its other side is redrawn on every move instead of floated, so a very large picture can feel a little heavier during that part of the drag.
Words flip about their stored box, which carries a few points of room on the far side, so mirrored words sit a couple of points off their outline.
A layer turned in 3D (Bring Nearer, a tilt) is flipped in its own plane; its 3D turn is left as it was rather than mirrored.
A shape, a line or a path is mirrored in its own points, so read_document shows no flip on it; a picture, words or a component copy report flipped.
